slides.title: Free-Energy-Gated Plasticity for Real-Time Online Motor Learning in Physical Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: REAL-TIME ONLINE MOTOR LEARNING VIA FREE-ENERGY-GATED PLASTICITY
slides.highlight: This work proposes Free-Energy-Gated Plasticity (FEGP) to enable robots to acquire new motor patterns during physical human-robot interaction while preserving previous learning, supporting RwB's focus on embodied learning.

card.one_liner: FEGP enables robots to learn multiple motor patterns online without forgetting, using free-energy-based plasticity regulation.
card.key_idea: Extends PV-RNN by scaling synaptic learning rates via a sigmoidal gate driven by variational free energy, which increases plasticity during model-environment mismatch and suppresses it during stability.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via prerecorded streams and real-time pHRI using a dual-arm robot. Metrics included repertoire coverage, retention, and DTW shape distance across 50 sessions.

slides.title: TacForcing: Streaming Action Generation with Execution-Time Tactile Feedback
slides.tldr: STREAMING ACTION GENERATION WITH TACTILE FEEDBACK
slides.highlight: TacForcing introduces a streaming action-generation framework and Execution-Aware Tactile Attention to incorporate real-time tactile feedback into contact-rich manipulation.

card.one_liner: TacForcing enables contact-rich manipulation by integrating real-time tactile feedback into a streaming action-generation framework.
card.key_idea: A Streaming Action Expert generates action blocks progressively, using Execution-Aware Tactile Attention (EATA) to condition only the next immediate block on current tactile feedback.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on six UniVTAC simulated tasks and three real-world tasks; achieved 65% and 69% average success rates, respectively, outperforming vision-only and reactive baselines.

slides.title: VISTA: Visually Inferred Spatial ConTact Attention for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: VISUALLY INFERRED CONTACT FEEDBACK FOR MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: VISTA-Policy uses a Visual Deformation Field to provide high-dimensional visuo-physical feedback for contact-rich tasks without requiring dedicated tactile sensors.

card.one_liner: VISTA enables contact-rich robot manipulation by using external cameras to infer gripper deformation as tactile feedback.
card.key_idea: A framework extracting a 3D Visual Deformation Field (VDF) from compliant grippers, using energy-based denoising and a relative incremental action space for imitation learning.
card.evaluation: Tested on grasping, unscrewing, and calligraphy tasks against DP3 and tactile baselines; showed superior success rates, sample efficiency, and OOD scale generalization.
card.limitation: Requires a compliant gripper whose structural deformation remains observable from an external camera.

slides.title: A Tendon-Driven Five-Fingered Hand with Distributed Tactile Perception for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.tldr: DEXTEROUS FIVE-FINGERED HAND WITH TACTILE SENSING
slides.highlight: This research introduces a tendon-driven five-fingered hand with a soft-rigid-hybrid structure and dual-modality tactile sensing. It is relevant to RwB for its application of embodied AI to complex humanoid manipulation and tactile perception.

card.one_liner: A tendon-driven five-fingered robotic hand combining a soft-rigid-hybrid structure with distributed dual-modality tactile sensing.
card.key_idea: A soft-rigid-hybrid tendon-driven design featuring distributed tactile elements on distal and middle phalanges to detect static contact and dynamic force variations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via manipulation experiments (counting gestures, pinching, grasping, and bottle-grasp recording) to demonstrate system feasibility.

slides.title: Robust Slip Detection and Material Classification via Spatiotemporal Transformers on a Uniformly-Illuminated Visuo-Tactile Sensor
slides.tldr: SENSORY FRAMEWORK FOR SLIP DETECTION AND MATERIAL CLASSIFICATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a visuo-tactile sensor and a dual-head TimeSformer network capable of high-precision depth reconstruction and fine-grained slip direction classification.

card.one_liner: A marker-less visuo-tactile sensor and framework for high-precision 3D reconstruction, slip detection, and material classification.
card.key_idea: Combines uniform RGB illumination to eliminate specular highlights with a dual-head TimeSformer for spatiotemporal slip tracking and ResNet-50 for static material recognition.
card.evaluation: Tested on 15 objects; achieved 95.5% state and 91.5% direction accuracy on unseen objects, and 98.8% material classification accuracy.

slides.title: GRAFT: Grounded and Efficient Online Reinforcement Adaptation for Fine-Grained Robot Manipulation
slides.tldr: EFFICIENT ONLINE VLA ADAPTATION FOR FINE-GRAINED MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: GRAFT improves the adaptation of vision-language-action policies for fine-grained tasks using grounded perception and cached prefix reuse. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction through enhanced robot manipulation capabilities.

card.one_liner: GRAFT enables efficient online VLA adaptation for fine-grained robot manipulation using grounded perception and cached states.
card.key_idea: Uses view-specific visual anchors trained with identity-free multi-region supervision and accelerates learning via frozen-prefix KV caching and single-step consistency action generation.
card.evaluation: Tested on four biomedical tasks with 45-minute budgets; GRAFT achieved 82.5% success, outperforming GRAFT-Union (57.5%) and increasing learner-update throughput up to 9.94x.
card.limitation: The policy is reactive and lacks explicit tracking of previous actions or task progress for long-horizon tasks.

slides.title: One-Shot Learning from Demonstration of Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation by Identifying Physical Interactions
slides.highlight: This work proposes a Learning from Demonstration method that explicitly models physical interactions to enable robust and adaptive reproduction of contact-rich tasks, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on physics-based skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: A one-shot LfD method for contact-rich manipulation using explicit physical interaction modeling.
card.key_idea: A hybrid position-force controller tracks demonstrated trajectories, triggering transitions based on identified contact-based conditions from a single demonstration.
card.evaluation: Real robot experiments (doors, locks, bolt screwing, dislodging, contouring) demonstrating robustness to geometric variations and online adaptation.

slides.authors: A. H. G. Overbeek et al.

slides.title: Leveraging Inter-object Affordances for Efficient Planning in Contact-rich Tasks
slides.highlight: This research introduces a method using Vision-Language Models to generate inter-object affordance abstractions, significantly improving planning success rates and speed for contact-rich robotic tasks.

card.one_liner: U-TAMP leverages VLM-generated inter-object affordances to efficiently plan contact-rich robotic tasks with heterogeneous objects.
card.key_idea: Extends Unified TAMP by using symbolic abstractions of physical interaction constraints (grasping, supporting, lifting, sliding) to guide heuristic search and minimize sub-symbolic reasoning.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in CoppeliaSim using kitchen organization tasks (2-5 objects). Compared against original U-TAMP and VLM-based planners on success rate and planning time.
card.limitation: Task success is highly sensitive to affordance detection accuracy; a few incorrect assignments can make stacking unfeasible.
